name: George
care_notes: Has an intolerance to poultry, possibly other ingredients too - must eat novel protein food. Currently eating venison canned food, which is widely available and non-prescription but a little pricey.
original_foster_description:
George is an absolute dream! He's affectionate, good-natured, confident, and social: he loves to be near his
humans and warms up to new people easily. He'll often sit in laps, especially at the dinner table, but other times
will chill independently. He's not shy about asking for pets with a gentle headbutt, and he particularly loves chin
rubs! And he chirps adorably when he wants attention. He's more mellow than playful, but he can get pretty
excited about wand toys at times! He has superb manners, enjoys scratching on his scratching post (not your
furniture!), stays off the counters, and uses the litter box perfectly.
George would be a sweet, calm, easygoing addition to a household with any level of cat experience. He has
specific ways he prefers to be petted (no belly rubs, please!) so he may not be good with very young children,
but would probably get along great with older kids as long as they respect his boundaries. I'm not sure if he'd
like to have a cat sibling, he seems like a dominant personality so may prefer to be king of the castle. But he
absolutely loves humans and is all-around a perfect pet! I mean, just look at this handsome guy 😍
He's a good eater, but gets an upset stomach from some common cat food ingredients (definitely poultry,
possibly other meats), so has to eat a novel-protein diet. He's doing great on venison-based wet food (Instinct
brand, which is widely available and non-prescription), with a little pumpkin mixed in for fiber - no digestive
issues as long as he sticks to this diet.

devotedly raised until they were weaned and ready for their own foster homes. Since then she has been able to
enjoy some kitten-hood of her own, as a young cat herself. She is playful at times, but overall pretty mellow. She

used to giving her kittens directions with little chirps, and is very communicative. She likes to be around people,
and will often plop down on your lap for a bath or nap. She can also be pretty independent, which is why we
think she could do well in a single cat home, as long as she gets the pampering and attention she needs and
deserves! Because she got along well with her kittens, we think she could also do well with the right cat
companion, but would likely need to be a mellow and easy going cat. She loves to sit on laps and be pet, but will
let you know when she has had enough, and can get overstimulated. She doesn’t really like to be held, but is
tolerant of most handling. She will play with claws occasionally, which we are working on, but is not aggressive.

we are saying!). While shy at first, especially around new sounds or spaces, she is extremely social and
definitely has a goofy side. She loves to lounge belly up with her legs splayed in every direction, and will spill

name: Seven
care_notes: Epilepsy - takes 1/4 pill (3.74 mg) phenobarbitol daily with food Prefers smoother wet-food textures; also eats dry food; soft stools after arrival reportedly resolved.
original_foster_description:
GENERAL: Seven likes playing, especially with her feather toy, and exploring new places like closets and under
beds. She generally dislikes being picked up or moved, but will certainly follow where you lead. She loves Churu
treats, which come in handy if she avoids her medicine while eating breakfast. She likes to knead soft textures
like a knitted blanket or cuddly stuffed animal. She also loves hunting something down, whether it's a toy, a
bottlecap you didn't know you lost, or your feet under the covers! Due to the latter, I will often let her roam the
rest of the house while I sleep, but she is always excited to come back for morning cuddles and playtime. She is
really silly and playful and will show you her belly sooner than most cats I know. She is generally confident and
social with new humans, but often prefers to be next to you rather than right on your lap or in your arms. I don't
know how she is with other cats or children, but I could see a playmate of either species being really good for
her, since she has a lot of energy for chasing and playing. If you are looking for a sweet and playful kitty who will
greet you with a purr and a flop each morning, Seven might be the perfect fit!
HEALTH: I have tried a few different foods for her, and while she generally enjoys eating wet food, she seems to
prefer the smoother or more consistent textures like pate or grilled. I tried the higher end tiki cat and weruva
brands but found that she will sometimes shy away from the bigger chunks in the "a jus" style. I also give her a
scoop of dry food each day, and she enjoys munching on it here and there - generally not all at once. I did
notice some soft stools in her litter after a week or so of her arrival here, but that has since resolved, so was
probably just her adjusting to the new environment and different foods.
BEHAVIOR: As for behavior, I noticed that she was more cuddly at first and since becoming more confident and
exploring the rest of the house she has become a little less willing to be picked up or sit on my lap. After a
couple weeks it also became clear that having her sleep in my bedroom wouldn't be possible because she really
likes to pounce on the blankets, with or without feet underneath. I will say that this morning she caught a mouse
in my room, so I do wonder if the behavior was related to her sensing that there was something to hunt and
catch nearby. (She dropped the mouse and I was able to release it outside.) I will let you know if I notice any
changes over the next few days, but she does seem more relaxed today.
